主要内容: DISH Network Corporation, through its subsidiary American H Block Wireless L.L.C., filed an application with the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to acquire all 176 H Block wireless spectrum licenses in Auction 96. The FCC's prohibition on certain communications related to the Auction expired on March 14, 2014. American won all 176 H Block Licenses with an aggregate bid of $1.564 billion, which concluded on February 27, 2014. However, the FCC has not issued the licenses yet, as the issuance depends on its review and approval of the application. DISH paid approximately $328 million to the FCC as a deposit on December 17, 2013, and the remaining balance of approximately $1.236 billion is due on March 28, 2014. If the FCC issues the licenses, DISH will also need to pay approximately $12.6 million to UTAM, Inc. and $94.9 million to Sprint Corporation for clearance costs. The 8-K filing by DISH Network Corporation on March 18, 2014, outlines the terms and conditions of the H Block Licenses, which are subject to specific build-out requirements. The licensee must provide signal coverage and offer service to at least 40% of the population in each area covered by an individual H Block License within four years of the FCC issuing the licenses. This is known as the H Block Interim Build-Out Requirement. If the licensee fails to meet this requirement, the license term and the H Block Final Build-Out Requirement may be accelerated by two years for each H Block License area in which it fails. The H Block Final Build-Out Requirement mandates that the licensee provide service to at least 75% of the population in each area covered by an individual H Block License within ten years. If the licensee fails to meet this requirement, its authorization for each H Block License area may terminate. The filing also highlights the potential need for significant investments or partnerships to finance the commercialization and build-out of any acquired H Block Licenses, as well as integration efforts and compliance with applicable regulations. The uncertainty surrounding the development and implementation of a business model for these licenses could affect the carrying value of potential assets and future financial condition.
